Definition: vegetable lye (from its cleansing); used as a soap for washing, or a flux for metals
BiblicalUsage: Lye is the word for potash, the alkali used to cleanse and to smelt — and it appears twice. In Isaiah 1:25 God says, I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin. In Job 9:30 Job says, if I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean — and the word for the cleansing is lye, the strong soap of the ancient world.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the lye in Isaiah is a hard mercy: God purges away the dross himself, because no washing of mine could do it.
